historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY27 Platform FUA guidance midpoint (165bn, avg FUA +21%) less ~2pp/yr platform revenue-margin compression (32bps -> ~30.5bps) plus Tech Solutions +8%: group revenue +17% in FY27, decelerating thereafter
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (2.7%) diverges >30% from revenue (21.1%) and EPS (46.9%) because HUB24 pays out ~46% of Underlying NPAT and spends ~55m/yr buying treasury shares; the 5yr equity CAGR (25.0%) is inflated by the FY22 Class scrip acquisition. Neither equity figure describes the business's growth, so the FUA-guidance-derived rate is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs use the continuing-operations series (RevenueContinuing; licensee business divested FY20). The 5yr figures span the FY22 Class acquisition (paid largely in shares) and overstate organic growth; FY26 organic revenue growth was 22.6%. Owner-FCF series = FCF - SBC - interest income (FY21 4.5m, FY23 44.5m, FY26 132.0m). The owner-FCF CAGR exceeds the reported-FCF CAGR because SBC has been flat at ~13-14m in dollars while FCF grew 2.7x since FY23 -- the opposite of the usual warning. FY17 net income (18.9m) included a 15.1m deferred-tax-asset recognition and is excluded from any margin averaging.

scenario_narratives.base: HUB24 keeps winning share from bank-owned platforms (BT Panorama, Macquarie Wrap, CFS, AMP North) as the #1 net-inflow platform, but FUA growth converts to revenue growth at roughly 0.85x because of admin-fee tiering. Revenue compounds 17% -> 4% over ten years, the pre-SBC EBITDA margin drifts from 41% to 45%, and SBC is charged at the settlement cost of the FY24-26 grants (5% of revenue) fading to 3%. Cash tax normalises to 29%. Net cash plus the 113.5m of loans and equity investments is added at book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Upper end of the FY27/FY28 FUA ranges with stable markets, revenue-margin compression limited to ~1pp/yr, the HUB24 Super trustee insourced by end-2026 capturing EQT's economics, myhub/Class cross-sell lifting Tech Solutions, and operating leverage taking the margin to 49%. Terminal growth 3.5% (the superannuation system compounds ~7%/yr structurally).
scenario_narratives.bear: A market drawdown in FY28-29 plus RBA cuts hit both ad-valorem and cash-margin revenue at the same time, revenue-margin compression accelerates under Netwealth competition and fee caps, and DBFO reforms let super funds deliver advice without a wrap platform. Growth stalls at 3-4%, the margin falls to 36.5%, and the business exits at 15x owner FCF. Not a solvency case: HUB24 has net cash, so the bear is a re-rating and margin case, not a survival one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF component DCF on a fee-earning custodial platform. Value is driven by (1) how much of the guided 15-20%/yr FUA growth survives fee tiering to reach revenue, (2) how far operating leverage takes a 41% pre-SBC margin, and (3) the true cost of equity compensation, which at HUB24 is the on-market treasury purchase (54-56m/yr) rather than the 13m grant-date expense. Interest & other income is stripped and the loan/equity investments that earn it are added back at book; leases are an operating cost and excluded from net debt; net cash is 41m. One 10% AUD WACC; cyclicality and fee compression live in the bear flows and a 25% bear weight.
key_risks_to_valuation: FUA is marked to market: an equity/bond drawdown and RBA cash-rate cuts reduce ad-valorem fees and cash-account margin simultaneously, without any change in adviser behaviour
Platform revenue margin (bps of FUA) is compressing 1-2bps/yr from fee tiering and caps; the base case assumes ~2pp/yr of growth leakage, the bear 3-4pp
SBC charged at 5% of revenue sliding to 3% is a judgment between the 2.7% grant-date expense and the 11-13% cash settlement cost of FY25-26; each 1pp of revenue is ~2-3% of value
Two-horse competition with Netwealth for the same finite pool of adviser-directed flows; growth is a share-transfer story
DBFO/QAR reform could route advised assets through super-fund channels that bypass wrap platforms
113.5m of related-party loans and minority equity stakes are added at book; the 77.5m HTFS loan supports the trustee being insourced and may be quasi-permanent capital
Terminal value is a large share of value at 10% WACC on a 45% margin; the 20x cap binds if Gordon exceeds it

inputs.sbc_source: HUB.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:4696 share-based payments expense incl. payroll tax (13,351 $'000); no net-share-settlement withholding disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0). Treasury shares purchased on-market to settle awards: 55.873m FY26, 54.0m FY25 (line 4895).
inputs.buyback_note: 55.873m is TreasurySharesPurchased -- on-market purchases to settle employee awards, i.e. the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat. There was no capital-return buyback in FY26; the only OnMarketBuyback was 12.493m in FY2024. Buybacks are value-neutral here because SBC is expensed.
inputs.share_count_basis: 81.502m ordinary shares net of 0.272m treasury shares at 30-Jun-26 (FY26 AR note 4.5.1) plus ~0.8m unvested performance rights; FY26 diluted weighted average was 82.091m (note 2.5.2). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the on-market treasury purchases are what funds the flat count.
inputs.sbc_treatment: Grant-date SBC expense is 2.72% of revenue (13.35m), but the cash actually spent buying shares on-market to settle vesting awards was 55.9m in FY26 and 54.0m in FY25 (11-13% of revenue) because the share price rose ~4x between grant and vesting. The forward sbc_pct_path is set at 5.0% in FY27 sliding to 3.0% by FY35: the FY24-FY26 grants (PARs struck at ~$40-90) vest over FY27-FY29 at roughly 2x grant-date fair value at today's price, and the charge converges to the expense as the price gap normalises. Same path in all three scenarios (risk charged once, in the growth/margin paths).
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows discounted at an AUD-built rate: AU 10yr ~4.3% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.1 => ~10.3% cost of equity; debt is 30m at BBSY+1.6% against a 5.7bn market cap, so WACC ~10.0%. One WACC across all three scenarios; cyclicality (FUA market beta, RBA cash-rate sensitivity) and fee compression are charged in the bear flows, not the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: B -- leases as operating cost. Full cash lease payment (FY26: 3.205m principal + 2.366m lease interest + 0.184m short-term = 5.76m; P&L cost 4.9m ROU depreciation + 2.4m interest = 7.3m after the FY25-26 office lease additions) deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (1.5% of revenue sliding to 1.2%). Lease liabilities (41.68m at 30-Jun-26) are EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is ex right-of-use depreciation and ex acquisition amortisation: 49.02 - 4.90 ROU - 24.5 acquisition = 19.6m = 4.0% of revenue, so the lease is not charged twice and the non-deductible Class/myprosperity/Xplore amortisation does not shelter cash tax.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- no non-controlling interests; statutory NPAT is 100% attributable.
inputs.ebitda_basis: ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC, POST-IFRS16 and EX interest & other income: FY26 Underlying EBITDA 211.4 less 10.2m interest & other income = 201.2m = 41.0% of revenue (FY25 39.0%, FY24 35.5%, FY23 36.3%). The CSV's statutory EBITDA (187.8) is that figure less SBC; SBC is charged separately by sbc_pct_path.
inputs.tax_note: FY26 cash tax 20.5m on 144.8m PBT (14%) and expense 24.6m (17%) versus 30% prima facie: 11.2m 'other deductible amounts' (largely the tax deduction on shares purchased to settle employee awards, which the engine captures by expensing SBC before tax) and 5.9m carry-forward losses/franking credits that are running off. Cash tax ramps 20% -> 29%; the residual 1pp below statutory is the structural ESS/R&D deduction.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year horizon (margin still ramping at year 5). HUB24 is a fee-earning custodial investment platform (Platform FUA $139.5bn off balance sheet, revenue 406.9m of admin/transaction/cash-margin fees) plus Tech Solutions (Class SMSF software, NowInfinity, myprosperity, 84.0m) -- an operating company, not a deposit-taker or REIT; EBITDA, FCF and net debt mean what the engine assumes. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). Interest & other income (10.2m: 8.5m interest received incl. 10% on the 77.5m HTFS trustee loan, plus Count dividends) is stripped from the flows and the source assets are added in the equity bridge at book (35.0m equity securities at FVOCI, 78.5m loans receivable) per the matching-asset rule. Owner FCF after the 3.2m lease principal = 128.8m. Analysis.json (2026-09-23) was read; FY27 Platform FUA guidance 160-170bn and the FY28 target 186-200bn anchor the growth path. Price is a live ASX intraday print, near the 52-week low (68.7-122.03); the stock is down ~27% YTD on margin-expansion moderation and fee-compression concerns despite record results.

bear.narrative: FY27 lands at the bottom of guidance (160bn) then an equity/bond drawdown in FY28-FY29 flattens FUA while RBA cuts squeeze the cash-account margin; fee tiering/caps and Netwealth price competition compress the revenue margin 3-4bps/yr instead of 1-2; DBFO reforms route some advised assets through super-fund channels that bypass wrap platforms. Revenue stalls at ~3-4% from FY29, the pre-SBC margin gives back 4pp to 36.5%, and the exit multiple is capped at 15x.

base.narrative: FY27 revenue +17% from the guided 160-170bn FUA range net of ~2pp/yr revenue-margin compression; FY28 +14% consistent with the 186-200bn target; then decelerating to 4% by FY36 as the share-gain runway from bank-owned platforms narrows. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin expands only 1pp in FY27 (management signalled moderating expansion) and plateaus at 45% by FY32. Cash tax ramps to 29%.

bull.narrative: Top of the FUA guidance/target ranges (170bn FY27, 200bn FY28) with steady markets and revenue-margin compression held to ~1pp/yr; the HTFS trustee insourcing captures the economics currently shared with EQT; Class/NowInfinity/myhub cross-sell lifts Tech Solutions to double-digit growth; operating leverage takes the pre-SBC margin to 49%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 25% because the two bear axes -- FUA is marked to market (a drawdown and RBA cuts hit fee and cash-margin revenue together) and platform revenue-margin compression is structural and already visible (32bps -> ~31bps, Morningstar's 'no moat' fair value ~$48) -- are macro-driven and outside management's control; the 27% YTD de-rating on a record year shows the market is already repricing that risk. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs several independent things (top of guidance, stable markets, EQT economics captured, myhub commercialising) to go right at once. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
